articles.title: Croc Delta Armor
articles.summary: Crocodile armor plates with dark water gloss and patina; organic scale shine, low contrast, spooky. A fine brick-wall or scale-row texture; at distance it shrinks to a faint horizontal-banded sheen in the highlight.
articles.what: Reference-backed dangerous animal overlay - swamp crocodile armor plates, bone teeth, dark water gloss, and river-patina scale texture remapped into dynamic M/R/CC spec r Up close: A neat running-bond brick grid of small rectangular plates, about 25 x 12 px, with thin bright mortar lines between them. Very faint on satin; on metallic each plate shows as a slightly raised tile with a bright seam in the highlight. From a distance: A fine brick-wall or scale-row texture; at distance it shrinks to a faint horizontal-banded sheen in the highlight. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Dangerous Animals (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Dangerous Animals", or search for "Croc Delta Armor".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and sides on metallic bases so the seams show
Combine with olive or swampy paint for the theme
Numbers stay readable; seams are thin and faint.
Faint plate seams in the highlight, easy to miss
Pairs well with: matte, gloss, metallic.
pitfalls: Not a croc skin paint pattern: it adds no green or brown colour
Not alligator crackle: plates are neat rectangles in rows, not irregular cells
Avoid: organic theme may clash with clean liveries, dark gloss hides detail on black.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
